I've been using Ubuntu 16.04 for one day now and decided to write a quick review. For the record, my system is an AMD Athlon quad-core, 2GB nVidia graphics card, 8GB RAM, 240GB SSD, & 1TB HDD. I did a clean install coming from 15.10 & am booting in UEFI mode.

Install

The installation went exactly as usual with the exception that it was much faster due to my new SSD*. (Woot!)

First run

The first run was actually rather disappointing. There is very little difference visually between 15.10 & 16.04; but I knew that going in. What was more substantial is the system crashed. A lot. It took me ~4 tries (read "hangs/sudden reboots) to get the first few additional programs installed & my backup restoring (due to adding a new SSD, I completely overwrote the old partitions). (Side note: DÃ©jÃ  Dup is amazing.) However, I am probably partly to blame for the crashes as I was messing around an awful lot (adding themes, installing a ton, adding PPAs, etc); stability has improved greatly since I stopped trying to "poke" & install everything at once.

Software Center

The new software center was another big let-down. It is much faster & cleaner than the old USC, but it is also missing features & programs. And it's buggy. Installing anything not in the default repos seems to be hit & miss. Steam (.deb file) simply refused to install & I had to revert to the terminal to install it. Other programs seemed to have issues requesting permissions; i.e. the authorization prompt wouldn't launch unless I was installing a program from the default repos. After the authorization was given, most programs installed just fine. I'm tempted to install the USC again, just so everything works smoothly but I realize that the new Ubuntu Software will likely improve greatly over the next few weeks.

Graphics, Themes, & Etc

I have had no problems with the graphics drivers. Both the nouveau driver & the proprietary nVidia driver are working with no hiccups (Steam still fails to run under the Nouveau driver).

The ability to move the launcher to the bottom is cool, but I really don't have a use for it. Widescreen monitors mean that vertical space is much more precious than horizontal space.

I installed the Arc theme from the OpenSuse 15.10 repo and it did work, however, it seemed to make things less stable. I haven't removed it but I did switch back to the default theme.

One annoying bug I've noticed is that with dual monitors, the second monitor does not go to sleep anymore. It does go blank but remains in full power state. I don't know if changing which monitor is primary would change the behavior to my other monitor or if it is determined by which port it is on (my secondary is plugged into the graphics card HDMI & using a passive HDMI to DVI converter). Edit: This bug stopped once I changed to the proprietary graphics driver.

There is a new option when right-clicking on the Files icon in the launcher; Show Copy Dialog. A very simple yet useful addition that will hopefully solve the "disappearing copy dialog" error. There are other tweaks to the right-click options but that is the one I've used so far.

I have yet to receive any updates.

TL;DR

Overall I am pretty happy with 16.04 but I'm anxious to start receiving updates to improve the overall stability.

*I'm trying a new setup where everything but /home is on the SSD & /home is on the HDD. So far, so good.
I had some crashes when installing programs through the new USC during the beta, was hoping they'd be fixed by release, I'll probably wait a bit before upgrading. Just to be certain.
